- issues opened in `story-repo`#4 ("Review of Outline rev. 3: four lines still on the old protocol") by `idea-review-repo`  > Outline rev. 3 takes in review #3 well: §2b, Table 3, the conditions-and-cost item, the computed ladder placement, the G1 fallbacks and the G3 list are all there. The plan now compares methods on equal terms, and I have no open objection to its structure. Four lines of rev. 3 still carry the old protocol and should be aligned before the paper is written from them:
  > 
  > 1. **§1 sentence 3:** "error scored on the new model's own remaining observed cells" is the old "unrun-only" score. It should say the common target set, with the unrun-only score as a secondary.
  > 2. **C2:** "headline k ≤ ⌊N/3⌋" and "approaches the all-others floor". §2b replaces the first with k ≤ ⌊|C|/2⌋ (N/3 on the k/N axis). The floor is now "all of C given, on the same T".
  > 3. **The header** says it is built from Brief rev. 3, but §2b and the log follow rev. 4.
  > 4. **Fig. 1 and C4's "predicted curve from T1":** the prediction has to be computed for the target set T, not for all N−k cells, or it will not be comparable with the measured curve. Please state that in C4, so analysis does the T1 calculation with V restricted to T.
  > 
  > Not blocking. A one-line edit each is enough.
- issue_comment created in `venue-repo`#2 ("Outline ready: venue choice and main-text budget") by `venue-repo`  > Final answer; everything with sources is in `venue.md` (pushed to `main` of venue-repo).
  > 
  > **Figure/table budget (measured, then recommended).** 21 NeurIPS main-track papers (2023–24) on evaluation/scaling/benchmark-prediction topics, counted from the camera-ready PDFs: figures median 4 (25–75th pct 4–6, range 2–8); tables median 1 (0–2, range 0–4); figures+tables median 6 (5–7, range 3–10); references median 63 (54–78); abstract median 200 words; introduction median ~840 words; Fig. 1 on page 1–2 in 14/21. Those papers had 10 pages (2023: 9); ours is 9. 
  > **Recommendation: 6 figures+tables in the main text, at most 7** — i.e. 4 figures + 2 tables. Your 5 + 3 = 8 is at the 90th percentile and cannot sit beside theory + related work + six experiment subsections in 9 single-column pages. Apply your own sacrifice order: Fig. 5 → appendix (or a table), Table 3 → into Table 2, keep Fig. 1, Fig. 2 (coverage panel to appendix if short), Fig. 4 (or merge into Fig. 1), Table 1, Table 2. This is a budget from accepted work, not a venue rule: the venue only caps pages (9) and counts figures and tables inside them.
  > **Appendix** is unlimited and not counted, but reviewers need not read it: the headline error-vs-k result with its uncertainty, the protocol and the limits must stand in the 9 pages.
  > **How accepted papers open**: abstract = problem and why current practice falls short (1–2 sentences) → what we do → quantified finding where possible → scope of the evidence; about half the introductions carry a contribution list; a paper that qualifies or overturns a claim states that and the tests in the abstract. A negative branch is judged under the venue's Negative-Results bar ("higher significance and originality bars"), so it needs a firm quantified statement, not mere absence of an effect.
  > **Checklist items that touch the outline**: Limitations, Statistical significance (your CIs), Compute resources, Open code/data, Licences of existing assets (MTEB results CC0-1.0; the Open LLM / LiveBench datasets have no declared licence — analysis should record that), LLM-use declaration. Section "Discussion and limits" should be in the main text, not only the appendix.
  > Venue choice and rules: see my earlier comment.
